events.description: Samuel Prindle: 4 males under 10, 1 male 26-44; 1 female under 10, 1 female 26-44. Next entry above: James Prindle: 2 males under 10, 1 male 10-15, 1 male 26-44; 3 females under 10, 1 female 10-15, 1 female 26-44.

bioAdditions:
The 1800 census of Plymouth Township lists 'James Prindle' and 'Samuel Prindle' one after the other, among the Lamoreaux, Steel, Van Loon and Davenport households (S1). Samuel's household (a man and a woman aged 26-44, four boys and one girl under 10) matches him, Martha and their young family (Thomas b. 1791, Benjamin b. 1794 and others), and James's household is very probably his brother James who married Phebe Lamoreux in 1785. This is direct evidence that both brothers came from Orange County to Plymouth.

On Samuel's parentage, two primary records bear on the FamilySearch claim that he was a son of James Prindle of Newtown, Connecticut. The Newtown church register records that 'James Prindle & Anar Turner both of Newtown' married on 22 January 1759 (S2), and the Barbour index card from Newtown Vital Records vol. 2 p.172 gives James Prindle's death as 9 December 1800 (S3; FamilySearch and the 1906 Prindle Genealogy say 9 Nov). Samuel (c.1767) and Hannah (1773) could be children of that marriage, but the FamilySearch sibling list also includes James (b. c.1754) and David (b. 1757), who were born before the 1759 marriage and therefore cannot be Anar Turner's children (S4). The FamilySearch family group is a reconstruction, not a documented family. Samuel's descent from James Prindle and Anar Turner stays speculative until a Newtown probate or deed record (James d. 1800) names him.

conflicts.foundValue: FamilySearch's family group includes sons born 1754 and 1757, before the parents' 22 Jan 1759 marriage
conflicts.assessment: The FS family is not internally consistent; parentage stays speculative.

openQuestionsNew: Newtown (CT) probate district file for James Prindle d. 9 Dec 1800 (Connecticut Wills and Probate, Ancestry; CSL probate packets): does it name Samuel 'of Luzerne County' or 'of Plymouth'?
Who was the James Prindle next door in 1800 (household with children up to 15, i.e. married by c.1785) - the James who married Phebe Lamoreux in 1785?

Prindles in the Hudson Valley before the move to Plymouth: a David Prindle lived at New Cornwall, Orange Co., in 1790, a few households from John Lomereaux and Oliver Davenport (1790 census, see Jean Lamoreaux I282695583838), and a Sgt. Moses Prindle served in Capt. Peter Harris's Dutchess Co. company in 1760 (NY Provincial Muster Rolls p.254). Check whether Samuel was in Orange Co. in the 1780s, before he married Martha Lamoreaux.

FamilySearch gives both Samuel Sr. (G99D-9DZ) and Samuel Jr. (KL4L-R8P) a death date of 25 Mar 1847, so one has been copied. No Samuel aged 70+ appears in the 1840 Plymouth Twp page that holds Benjn, Saml (30-40) and James Pringle; look for Samuel Sr. elsewhere in 1840 (Kingston Twp?).
